desc:
A theatre has rows rows, numbered from 1, and every row has 10 seats numbered 1 to 10. The entry reserved[i] = [row, seat] is a seat that is already taken.

A group of four people must sit together on four consecutive seats of one row. Because of the aisles, the only blocks of seats a group may use are 2-5, 4-7 and 6-9. Two groups cannot share a seat, and no group may use a reserved seat.

Return the maximum number of groups that can be seated in the whole theatre.

rows = 4, reserved = [[1,2],[1,8],[2,6],[3,1],[3,10]]  -> 6
rows = 2, reserved = []                                -> 4

In the first example row 1 fits one group (seats 4-7), row 2 fits one (seats 2-5), row 3 fits two (2-5 and 6-9) and row 4 is empty and fits two.
hints: Rows are independent. How many groups can one row hold at most, given the three allowed blocks?
Blocks 2-5 and 6-9 do not overlap, so a row fits two groups exactly when both of them are free. Block 4-7 overlaps both.

Per row: two groups if blocks 2-5 and 6-9 are both free, otherwise one group if any of the three blocks is free, otherwise zero. Rows without reservations contribute 2 each and must not be looped over one by one.
editorial: Only rows that appear in reserved need work. Collect the reserved seats of each such row. The left block 2-5 is free when no reserved seat lies in 2..5, the right block 6-9 when none lies in 6..9, and the middle block 4-7 when none lies in 4..7.

If left and right are both free the row takes two groups. Otherwise the row takes one group if the middle, the left or the right block is free (they all overlap pairwise), else none. Add 2 * (rows - number of rows with reservations) for the untouched rows. Time O(m) for m reservations, independent of the number of rows. The maximum answer 2 × 109 still fits into 32 bits.
